disease_label_per_paper: Massive amebic liver abscess in uncontrolled diabetes mellitus with concurrent pulmonary embolism
presentation_summary: 61-year-old man originally from Nigeria with hypertension and uncontrolled diabetes mellitus presented in the United States with persistent right upper quadrant pain radiating to the back and dark urine.
He had no recent nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or travel outside the United States in the prior two years.
Exam showed tachycardia to 117/min, fever to 100.8 F, conjunctival icterus, and right upper quadrant tenderness.
Admission labs showed hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL, random glucose 438 mg/dL, HbA1c 13.6%, ALP 587 U/L, total bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, AST 202 U/L, and ALT 245 U/L.
Ultrasound showed a large complex cystic right-lobe lesion measuring 14.39 x 6.55 cm; CT abdomen/pelvis characterized a 13.93 x 9.17 cm lesion compatible with a giant liver abscess.
The patient was initially treated for possible pyogenic abscess with cefepime/vancomycin, then ceftriaxone/metronidazole after CT review and CT-guided drainage.
A subsequent CT incidentally detected a right lower lobe pulmonary embolus without DVT or hepatic/portal vein thrombosis on Doppler.
E. histolytica serology later returned positive, paromomycin was added, and CT at three months showed near-complete abscess resolution.

quality_warnings: The paper does not report WBC, CRP, blood cultures, abscess culture, or abscess aspirate appearance; these were not invented.
